replacement.headline: Fact-check: A foreign state broadcaster mocks the port closure. Here's what officials actually say.
replacement.dek: A state-run outlet abroad is calling the Corpus Christi channel closure a sign of U.S. weakness. What's confirmed: an explosive device, an active Navy and Coast Guard search, and an FBI investigation.
body: THE CLAIM: A foreign state broadcaster is airing segments that mock the closure of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel as a sign of American weakness. One segment called it "a harbor America cannot even keep open."

WHAT'S CONFIRMED: The channel is closed. The Navy said Saturday that Thursday's blast beside the harbor tug Corrin Bay near the Port Aransas jetties was caused by an explosive device. Navy explosive ordnance disposal and mine countermeasures teams are searching the channel with the Coast Guard. The FBI is investigating. Two tug crew members were injured.

WHAT THE BROADCAST LEAVES OUT: Closing a channel after an explosion is a safety decision, and the Coast Guard made it within hours. "Closing the channel is how you keep people safe while you find out what happened," said Lt. Cmdr. Elena Ruiz, a public affairs officer for Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi. "That's the system working."

WHY IT MATTERS: Misleading posts spread fast after a disaster. Since Hurricane Rafael, false claims about the military seizing homes have circulated locally, and county and base officials have debunked them. Whatever the source, mocking or misleading messages work the same way: they want you angry, and they want you to share.

WHAT TO DO: Don't share clips from foreign state media, even to argue with them; sharing spreads them. Get updates from the Coast Guard, the Navy and local news. Harborline 6 is not naming or linking the outlet. If a clip reaches you, check who made it and when before you react.

replacement.headline: Navy: explosive device caused Texas port blast
replacement.dek: The blast that closed the Corpus Christi Ship Channel was caused by an explosive device, the Navy said Saturday. Officials have not said who placed it.
body: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (Continental Wire) — The explosion that damaged a harbor tug and closed one of the nation's most important energy ports was caused by an explosive device, the Navy said Saturday, as Navy explosive ordnance disposal and mine countermeasures teams searched the Corpus Christi Ship Channel alongside the Coast Guard.

An explosive device caused the blast near the jetties, said Cmdr. Lisa Moreau, a public affairs officer for Navy Region Southeast. "Our teams are searching the channel with the Coast Guard, and safety comes first," she said. The FBI said it is investigating.
Officials have not said who placed the device, when or why.
Loadings at the port, the source of about half of U.S. crude exports, are halted again, and traders are watching for a prolonged closure. No reopening date has been announced.

The Defense Department counts the Port of Corpus Christi among its designated strategic seaports. A Fort Hood aviation brigade had been scheduled to move its helicopters and equipment through the port for what the Army has described only as an overseas rotation. The movement was postponed before Hurricane Rafael and, the Army said Friday, has been delayed again by the channel closure. "The brigade will be ready to go as soon as the channel is," said Maj. Darnell Price, a Fort Hood public affairs officer.

The blast, around 1 a.m. Thursday near the jetties at Port Aransas, damaged the tug Corrin Bay and injured two crew members. The channel had partly reopened only two weeks earlier, after a month-long closure caused by the hurricane.
